answer: In an agent economy, a credential issuer could place one secret per verified person in a private vault. Each reward round requires a proof yielding the same round-specific nullifier for that person, so aliases can wander between wallets but cannot claim twice. An ivory badge on the interface is only decoration; uniqueness comes from verification and duplicate rejection. Attackers must recruit or steal additional identities. Corrupt issuers, identity rental and exclusion of undocumented people remain limits.
